postings.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Data Curation & Dataset Strategy
postings.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.



We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.



Here’s what this particular role covers.



🛠️ About our datasets Team

Wayve's datasets team own the driving data that our AI Driver learns from, covering ingestion, annotation, retrieval and data quality. As our data grows from hundreds of petabytes towards exabyte scale, deciding what we keep, and where, is one of the biggest levers on both model quality and cost. This role sits at the centre of that challenge, shaping the data that model engineers train on across the company.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

 - Build and own the ingestion-time model that scores incoming driving data and routes it to hot, cold, archive or delete

 - Work with training teams to define the right data distributions for every model we're building

 - Deliver early storage-cost savings through practical heuristics, then develop ML-driven filtering

 - Partner with ingestion, annotation, retrieval, data quality, model training, AV/robotics, evaluation and storage teams to set company-wide data policy

 - Lead and work hands-on with a small group of software and ML engineers to build data provisioning and data provenance features into Corpus

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

 - Defining our dataset content strategy: which data and metadata we need, and why, so training teams can select the most valuable data as smoothly as possible

 - Steering data selection by what our model engineers need right now. For example, if we're weak at unprotected right turns at traffic lights, those scenarios go straight to hot storage

 - Delivering large, measurable storage-cost savings as ingestion scales across our internal fleet and partner and OEM data

 - Evolving from practical heuristics to ML-driven filtering, and influencing what gets filtered at the vehicle and edge

 - Working as a pair with our Corpus Implementation Engineer to turn strategy into production systems

 

🙌 You should apply if

 - You have strong autonomous-vehicle or robotics experience, working with large-scale driving, sensor or comparable data

 - You're a principal, hands-on ML engineer who has built models that score, select or filter data

 - You've operated at petabyte scale and are comfortable with the engineering that comes with it

 - You're strong in Python and Spark, with large-scale cloud data experience

 - You have strong quantitative intuition and use it to make practical, measurable decisions

 - You're pragmatic and high-ownership, and can set direction across several teams without direct authority

 - You bring experience in data selection, retention or filtering for model training, edge or vehicle-side filtering, computer vision or high-volume IoT data, or leading small cross-functional groups (any of these is a bonus)

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

 - Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

 - Intro with the hiring manager (1 hour)

 - Competency interviews: system design and technical leadership (2 hours total)

 - Deep dive: domain interview (1 hour)

 - Final interview: mission & values alignment (1 hour)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

 

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more



A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.



If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.


For more information visit Careers at Wayve. https://wayve.ai/careers/ To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve https://wayve.ai/careers/

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

postings.title: Senior Software Engineer - Runtime Platform, Robot Software
postings.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.



We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.



Here’s what this particular role covers.



🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

Wayve’s Robot Software team builds the software that runs across our internal vehicle fleet, enabling autonomous driving and collecting the data used to train new driving models. We deliver a reliable, stable, and flexible software stack that allows model developers and scientists to run on-road experiments, iterate quickly, and bring new autonomous-driving capabilities to life.

The Runtime Platform team owns the shared foundations that the onboard software stack depends on: application frameworks, communication middleware, application lifecycle management, system health monitoring, performance, and observability. We build reusable runtime capabilities that help engineering teams develop and operate reliable software across different vehicles, operating systems, and compute platforms.

As a Software Engineer, Runtime Platform, you’ll develop shared runtime software, investigate end-to-end performance, and help guide architectural decisions across Robot Software. Your work will help the onboard stack meet its latency, throughput, reliability, and resource requirements as it evolves and moves onto new platforms.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

 - Design, build, and maintain shared onboard application frameworks and developer interfaces.

 - Develop application lifecycle management, health monitoring, fault reporting, and runtime diagnostics.

 - Evolve Wayve’s communication middleware by evaluating technologies, migrating components, and supporting new operating systems and compute platforms.

 - Investigate latency and performance bottlenecks across the full onboard software stack.

 - Instrument software with profiling tools and metrics to identify optimisation opportunities.

 - Collaborate with engineering teams to understand performance pain points and prioritise improvements by impact.

 - Work with internal teams and middleware suppliers to resolve integration issues and establish shared APIs, documentation, and best practices.
   
   

🧩 What you’ll be working on

 - Shared runtime services and application frameworks used across Robot Software.

 - Communication middleware and high-throughput, low-latency inter-process communication.

 - End-to-end profiling across OS scheduling, memory hierarchy, CPU caches, context switching, thread synchronisation, and critical code paths.

 - New profiling and instrumentation tools for benchmarking system performance and establishing baselines.

 - Automated benchmarks and CI checks that detect performance regressions and validate runtime behaviour across supported platforms.

 - Ports and integrations across new operating systems, vehicle compute, and hardware platforms.

 - Observability infrastructure for logs, metrics, traces, and fleet-level performance analysis.

 

🙌 You should apply if

 - You have strong software-development experience in C++.

 - You are proficient with performance-profiling tools and techniques for finding and resolving system bottlenecks.

 - You have a proven, methodical approach to designing experiments and evaluating results.

 - You have a strong foundation in OS scheduling, computer architecture, memory hierarchy, CPU caches, context switching, and thread synchronisation.

 - You have developed or maintained middleware, application frameworks, communication infrastructure, lifecycle management, or shared runtime services.

 - You can design maintainable interfaces and help multiple engineering teams integrate and adopt shared software components.

 - You can collaborate across teams to turn performance data into clear architectural and optimisation decisions.

Deep experience with communication middleware or application-framework design would be especially valuable. Experience porting systems software across operating systems and hardware platforms, building automated performance benchmarks in CI, or using NVIDIA tools such as Nsight, Lumos, and tegrastat is also relevant. Familiarity with Grafana, Databricks, Datadog, QNX, or Momentics is a plus.

Our Customer Integration Engineers sit close to our automotive partners, supporting them from the first integration through to final validation of Wayve's technology. Based near customer sites, the team bridges customer vehicle integration teams and Wayve's internal engineering teams, so issues are diagnosed in real time and resolved quickly. 



🧠 Your day-to-day

 - Provide hands-on technical support to customers throughout development and validation

 - Run rapid diagnostics alongside customer engineering teams and identify issues in real time

postings.title: Purchasing Manager
postings.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.



We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.



Here’s what this particular role covers.




PURCHASING MANAGER



🛠️ About our Purchasing Team

Wayve’s Purchasing team helps the business scale by ensuring we have the right suppliers, commercial agreements, and procurement processes in place to support our global operations.

As an Indirect Purchasing Manager, you’ll help shape how Wayve sources, manages, and optimizes indirect spend across areas including IT/SaaS, Marketing, People/HR, Facilities, and Security. You’ll work closely with teams across the business to identify the right suppliers, negotiate strong commercial terms, manage risk, and ensure our supplier relationships continue to deliver value as Wayve grows.

This is an opportunity to have a direct impact on how we build a scalable, efficient, and commercially strong procurement function in a fast-moving global environment.



🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll own procurement activities across a broad range of indirect categories, partnering with internal stakeholders to understand their requirements and develop sourcing strategies that balance cost, quality, service, and risk.

You’ll manage the end-to-end supplier and contract lifecycle — from identifying and evaluating suppliers through negotiation, contracting, onboarding, performance management, renewal, and escalation.

You’ll work closely with Legal, Finance, HR/People, IT, Security, Facilities, and Marketing to ensure purchasing decisions align with business priorities and company policies. You’ll also help improve procurement processes, strengthen supplier governance, and use spend and performance data to identify opportunities for savings and greater efficiency.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

 - Developing and executing indirect procurement and sourcing strategies aligned with business priorities and cost-efficiency targets.

 - Managing sourcing activities across categories including IT/SaaS, Marketing, People/HR services, Facilities, Security, and other corporate services.

 - Leading supplier identification, evaluation, competitive sourcing, and commercial negotiations.

 - Owning supplier contracts from initial negotiation and drafting through execution, renewal, and ongoing compliance management.

 - Negotiating and managing commercial agreements including MSAs, SOWs, NDAs, order forms, and supplier terms, in partnership with Legal.

 - Building and maintaining strong relationships with global suppliers and monitoring performance, service quality, risk, and compliance.

 - Managing contract renewals and identifying opportunities to improve commercial terms, consolidate suppliers, or reduce unnecessary spend.

 - Acting as the key point of contact between suppliers and internal stakeholders for commercial issues, escalations, and performance concerns.

 - Analyzing spend data, supplier KPIs, market trends, and commercial benchmarks to support sourcing decisions.

 - Supporting budget planning and forecasting across indirect spend categories.

 - Implementing and improving procurement best practices, including supplier scorecards, spend tracking, contract lifecycle management, and governance.

 - Ensuring procurement activities comply with internal policies, ethical sourcing standards, and risk-management requirements.



🙌 You should apply if:

 - You have 5+ years of experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier management, or a related purchasing role.

 - You have experience managing indirect spend categories, ideally including IT/SaaS, Marketing, Facilities, People/HR services, Security, or other corporate services.

 - You have strong end-to-end supplier contract management experience, including negotiation, contract review, execution, renewals, and ongoing vendor management.

 - You understand global procurement practices, supplier governance, compliance, and third-party risk management.

 - You have experience partnering closely with Legal, Finance, HR, IT, Security, and other business stakeholders in a matrixed or global organization.

 - You are a confident commercial negotiator who can balance cost, quality, business requirements, and supplier risk.

 - You have strong communication and stakeholder-management skills and are comfortable influencing across different functions and levels of seniority.

 - You are analytical and comfortable using spend data, supplier performance metrics, benchmarks, and KPIs to make informed decisions.

 - You are highly organized and able to manage multiple sourcing initiatives, contracts, renewals, and supplier relationships at the same time.

 - You are comfortable operating in a fast-paced, dynamic environment where priorities can change quickly.

 - Experience with procurement or contract-management platforms such as SAP Ariba, Coupa, Ivalua, Oracle Procurement Cloud, or similar tools would be beneficial.

postings.description:

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

📊 About our Data Quality & Provenance Team 

Our Data Quality & Provenance team sits within Wayve’s AI Platform organisation and builds the evidence that helps teams make confident decisions about the data underpinning our embodied AI systems. We develop statistically robust methods, metrics and tools to determine when data-quality, annotation and evaluation signals can be trusted—and when they cannot. 

🧠 Your day-to-day 

 - Define measurable, statistically rigorous concepts of data quality, including coverage, label quality, uncertainty, provenance and model performance.

 - Apply statistical-inference methods to multi-rater annotation, label ambiguity, dataset coverage and black-box model evaluation.

 - Partner with annotation, autonomy and evaluation teams to translate practical quality questions into defensible metrics.

 - Build automated reports that clearly communicate confidence, limitations and appropriate interpretation.

 - Analyse large annotation datasets using Python and SQL to identify quality issues and inform decisions.

 - Iterate on metrics and reporting based on feedback from the teams using them.

 🧩 What you’ll be working on

 - Statistical methods for distinguishing genuine data-quality problems from label ambiguity, inconsistent annotation or evaluation noise.

 - Labeler and dataset metrics that support training-data selection, simulation, annotation acceptance and model evaluation.

 - Reusable quality artefacts that replace one-off analyses with registered, automated metrics and reports.

 - Multi-rater and human-in-the-loop ML systems, including approaches such as Dawid–Skene-style models, psychometrics and inter-rater agreement.

 - Quality standards spanning coverage, uncertainty, provenance, annotation quality and predictive-model performance.

 - Integration of data-science outputs into the platform workflows used by engineering and research teams

 - You have strong foundations in classical statistics, including experimental design, sampling, modelling, estimation and inference.

 - You have practical experience with rater or annotator modelling, inter-rater agreement, label uncertainty or related methods. 

 - You understand data quality across dimensions such as coverage, label quality, uncertainty, provenance and model performance.

 - You have worked with annotation tooling, QA methodologies, human-in-the-loop ML systems or multi-rater labelled datasets.

 - You have strong Python and SQL skills and are confident analysing large, complex datasets.

 - You can turn ambiguous stakeholder questions into rigorous, usable metrics and clearly communicate uncertainty, limitations and decision implications.

 - Summarising, visualising and communicating findings in an accessible way that supports prioritisation and strategy.

 - Offline perception work using additional inputs not viable for on-road production, including extra sensors like lidar, future frames, maps, and extra compute, to improve data quality and coverage at scale

postings.description:

🛠️ About our Simulation Teams

Generative Simulation is the team advancing our end-to-end autonomous driving research, incubating and investing in new ideas that can become game-changing technological advances for Wayve. As a Machine Learning Engineer in the team, you will play a key role in developing next-generation world models and planners, such as GAIA, that can simulate complex, diverse, and temporally consistent driving environments to power faster training, broader testing, and scalable deployment, even in areas and scenarios we have never driven in before. As we push toward the next generation of GAIA, efficiency and interactivity are a major focus: models must run thousands of roll-outs per second, support closed-loop agent interaction, and fit within practical compute budgets. You will work at the intersection of machine learning research, multi-modal modelling, and real-world deployment, tackling questions such as how we can deploy autonomous vehicles in a new geography without collecting any real-world data, and whether synthetically generated environments can fully replace physical testing and data collection.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

 - Setting technical direction: Set technical direction and designing key components of the system.

 - Deep work / coding: You spend a focused block implementing and debugging new modeling capabilities.

 - Cross-team collaboration, brainstorming and pairing: you brainstorm ideas with your team mates or pair to solve a difficult problem

 - Mentorship / async review: You review a teammate’s pull request or experimental design and outcomes and provide feedback

 - Sync-ups: Share findings with the rest of your team leading to a discussion on designing the next experiments. You align on shared priorities for the week and blockers.

 - Paper reading/ reading groups: Read one of the latest papers and summarise them for yourself or the team to present in the next reading group if interesting

 - Ship impact: integrate your models into closed-loop training and evaluation, and measure the sim-to-real gap against on-road driving-model results.

 - Mentor and influence: guide junior researchers, shape technical road-maps, publish at top venues and represent Wayve in the community.

 - Challenge assumptions and drive innovation: propose bold ideas, conduct ablation studies, and question conventional approaches to training and evaluation.

postings.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.



We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.



Here’s what this particular role covers.



SUPPLY CHAIN PROGRAMME MANAGER

🛠️ About our Supply Chain Team

The Supply Chain Programme Manager is a critical cross-functional role responsible for owning end-to-end supply chain execution across assigned programmes and product builds at Wayve. This includes prototype development, new product introduction (NPI) and supporting fleet launches.

You’ll serve as the primary Supply Chain lead for your programmes, ensuring programme deliverables, supplier compliance and seamless coordination across Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing and external partners. You’ll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Planning, Sourcing, Logistics, Finance, Legal and Suppliers, while partnering closely with global upfitters and third-party integration partners across the US, UK and other regions to ensure vehicle and programme timelines are met.


🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll own end-to-end material readiness across assigned programmes, translating engineering requirements and demand into procurement plans and identifying supply risks early in the product lifecycle.

You’ll operate as the strategic liaison between hardware engineering and procurement, coordinating internal teams, suppliers, upfitters and integration partners to keep builds moving. This role combines strategic programme ownership with hands-on execution in a fast-moving, hardware-driven environment.


🧩 What you’ll be working on:

 - Acting as the primary Supply Chain lead for assigned programmes and internal product builds, including prototypes, NPI and subassemblies.

 - Owning end-to-end material readiness to support programme milestones across R&D, Engineering, Operations and Manufacturing.

 - Collaborating with Engineering, Planning, Sourcing, Logistics, Finance and Suppliers to align supply chain activities with programme timelines.

 - Acting as the strategic liaison between hardware engineering and procurement teams, including managing demand aggregation.

 - Translating engineering BOMs and aggregated Technical Programme Manager demand into procurement plans.

 - Identifying long-lead items and critical-path components early in the product lifecycle.

 - Tracking material status throughout build phases and proactively escalating gaps and risks.

 - Serving as the primary programme manager for upfitter and partner relationships, ensuring alignment across stakeholders.

 - Driving upfitter and partner activities to ensure vehicles meet overall programme timelines and quality standards.

 - Proactively identifying and resolving issues affecting vehicle build readiness, coordinating between internal teams and external partners.

 - Maintaining clear communication cadences with upfitters and stakeholders, tracking milestones and escalating risks as needed.

 - Defining, tracking and reporting key supply chain performance metrics, including material availability, total cost savings and inventory cycle count accuracy.

 - Establishing programme-level supply chain dashboards and reporting cadences to provide leadership and cross-functional stakeholders with visibility.

Wayve ships a new driving model baseline every week. The Model Integration & Release team runs simulation and on-road testing to decide whether model candidates are ready to promote. As our release process matures, we have an opportunity to learn more from the data we already collect: strengthening how we measure performance, turning on-road findings into better simulation tests, and aligning what we measure with what operators experience in the vehicle.

As a Senior Data Scientist on the Model Integration & Release team, you will own this analytical layer. You will turn evaluation outputs into findings that improve both our models and how we measure them, working across simulation, on-road experiment data, and internal evaluation tooling. You will partner with Validation, Data Science, and Product to improve how we evaluate and make release decisions more confident.



🧠 Your day-to-day

You will lead analysis of model and autonomous-vehicle performance data, translating complex signals from simulations, offline evaluation, and on-road testing into clear recommendations for engineering teams. You will investigate performance issues, apply statistical rigour to evaluation data, and identify where our metrics, test coverage, or scoring logic could be improved.

You will work autonomously in a fast-moving weekly release cadence, prioritising analysis work, partnering across teams, and turning investigations into durable improvements.

 - Investigate on-road release-test findings, determine whether offline tests should have caught them, and improve evaluation coverage and measurement.

 - Perform experiment analysis and apply statistical methods to provide confident, data-driven promotion recommendations for new driving models.

 - Expand what “good” means beyond intervention rates, using the behavioural and operational signals we already collect.

 - Partner with Data Science and Validation on how evaluation methods and ground truth are defined, implemented, and maintained.

 - Support partner-facing quality investigations by quantifying and tracking issues raised through OEM QA workflows.

 - Document findings and recommendations in a way the team can act on within a weekly release cadence, and follow through so the same class of issue does not recur.

 - You have experience applying statistical methods for A/B testing and experimentation, including confidence intervals, distributions, and sampling.

 - You are proficient in Python or SQL and comfortable querying and analysing large datasets.

 - You can operate with autonomy in a fast-moving environment: setting priorities within a broader goal and knowing when to solve an issue directly versus when to escalate or partner.

🛡️ About our Safety Team

As Technical Director, Safety Case, you’ll own the architecture, strategy and integrity of Wayve’s safety cases for our first products. The role sits independently from Engineering and Product and reports into Safety Management & Assurance, providing senior expert safety oversight while working closely with the teams responsible for designing, developing, validating and releasing our products.

You’ll act as the architect of the safety case—defining the top-level claims, argumentation structure, evidence strategy and assurance approach that connect product intent, system behaviour, AI performance, engineering controls, validation and operational deployment into a coherent safety argument.


🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll provide independent challenge and advice while enabling Engineering and Product teams to own and deliver the safety evidence required for their systems. You’ll move between top-level safety strategy and detailed technical evidence, identifying gaps and weak assumptions early enough to influence product decisions.

You’ll work across Product, Systems Engineering, AI/ML, Validation, Vehicle Engineering, Software, Hardware and Operational Safety to ensure requirements, architectures, validation plans and release criteria remain aligned with the safety case. You’ll also provide senior leadership and safety governance forums with an independent, evidence-based view of whether the safety argument is sufficiently strong to support release and deployment decisions.


🧩 What you’ll be working on:

 - Owning the safety case strategy and architecture for Wayve’s robotaxi and OEM ADAS products.

 - Defining top-level safety claims, argumentation, evidence structures and traceability from safety requirements through validation and deployment decisions.

 - Developing safety arguments appropriate for AI-enabled autonomous driving, incorporating functional safety, SOTIF, AI safety, cybersecurity, validation, operational safety and post-deployment monitoring.

 - Evolving reusable safety case approaches as Wayve’s products, vehicle platforms and evidence base mature.

 - Partnering with Product, Systems Engineering, AI/ML, Validation, Vehicle Engineering, Software, Hardware and Operational Safety to define safety requirements and evidence expectations.

 - Identifying gaps, assumptions and weaknesses in the safety argument early and driving their resolution with accountable teams.

 - Ensuring product requirements, architecture, validation plans and release criteria remain aligned with the safety case.

 - Supporting technical and programme leaders in making proportionate, evidence-based safety decisions.

 - Providing independent technical challenge of safety cases and supporting evidence.

 - Assessing whether safety arguments are coherent, complete, evidence-backed and sufficient to support release or deployment.

 - Highlighting material gaps, uncertainties, dependencies, residual risks and safety red lines, and providing clear recommendations to safety governance forums and senior leadership.

 - Building a common understanding of safety case principles across Wayve and coaching Engineering and Product leaders on structured safety argumentation, evidence quality and traceability.

 - Representing the safety case perspective in internal governance, customer and technical discussions.

 - Contributing to Wayve’s broader safety strategy and assurance capability.

Wayve’s safety argument for AI-enabled autonomous driving will be technically rigorous, scalable and capable of standing up to scrutiny from customers, regulators and independent assessors.

 - You have demonstrated the ability to translate complex technical evidence into structured safety claims and arguments.

postings.description:

Simulation is advancing end-to-end autonomous driving research. The team’s mission is to accelerate AV2.0 by incubating capabilities that become company-level advantages — generative world models and the synthetic data they produce are one of those. The goal of this role is to build, scale, and optimise next-generation world model architectures (GAIA and successors) and bridge them into high-throughput generation and training infrastructure, so synthetic data can dramatically accelerate autonomy development. You will post-train world models for new embodiments and behaviours (rig transfer, pose transfer, dashcam restaging), generate multimodal synthetic experience at scale, and land that data in the same training stack we use for real driving. You sit between ML research and engineering: collaborating with scientists on architecture and conditioning, and with platform engineers on generation jobs, training artefacts, and how synthetic data is mixed into training. Your work will decide how fast we can train, evaluate, and deploy driving models on vehicles we have barely collected from.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

 - Model development: Post-train, distill, and evaluate GAIA-family large video diffusion models to improve generation quality, controllability, and generalisation. Run ablation studies and investigate failures in visual quality, temporal consistency, motion, and action conditioning.

 - Generation at scale: Build and run synthetic video generation pipelines across tens of thousands of driving segments. Optimise inference efficiency, manage GPU resources, and ensure data quality throughout the pipeline.

 - From generation to training: Integrate synthetic data across different stages of driving-model training, develop sampling strategies, and measure its impact through evaluation suites and on-road performance.

 - Cross-team collaboration: Work with driving-model teams to determine effective data mixtures and with simulation and evaluation teams to turn generated scenarios into useful closed-loop tests.

 - Improve throughput and yield: inference optimisations (distillation, KV cache), valid-generation rate, and self-serve workflows so model developers can request synthetic sets without a specialist.

 - Expand coverage to new vehicle platforms and safety-critical scenarios (OEM bring-up; Emergency Lane Keeping / Automatic Emergency Braking).

 - Partner with world-model researchers, infra, and driving-model owners so generation, evaluation, and training stay one system.

 - 4+ years in applied ML / research engineering, with a track record of training and shipping neural nets, not only operating data platforms.

 - Strong Python and PyTorch (or equivalent); comfort with GPU training, debugging, and reading model code.

 - Hands-on experience with video, generative, or world models (diffusion / flow-matching / autoregressive video, novel-view synthesis, neural rendering, or similar).

 - Evidence of taking generated or simulated data into a trained downstream model and measuring impact (mix, ablations, failure analysis).

As part of a newly established function within Fleet Operations, the Field Engineer will help refine processes and drive efficiency in a fast-paced, high-impact environment.

Here’s what this particular role covers.



🛠️ About our Robotics Team

The Robotics team is responsible for bridging the gap from our model to our vehicle platforms, in order to let the model focus on making driving decisions. We aim to provide high quality data to the model for making such decisions, whilst abstracting away platform-specific aspects.



🧠 Your day-to-day

 - Lead the development of MVPs that unblock high-priority internal use cases, while guiding the transition to a robust internal platform.

 - Establish the core technical interfaces, output representations, and tools needed to support internal customers.

 - Partner with calibration, sensor fusion, perception, data, infrastructure, and validation teams to align requirements, resources and ownership boundaries.

 - Communicate technical tradeoffs, limitations, and progress clearly to engineering leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.



🧩 What you’ll be working on:

Leading the development of an offline 3D reconstruction capability that builds high-quality 3D world geometry from vehicle sensor data in dynamic scenes. The system will draw on localization and mapping, state estimation, and sensor fusion to produce offline 3D geometric reconstructions and best-estimate ego motion from heterogeneous vehicle platforms and sensor suites. The work will support internal validation, data enrichment, and model development by turning raw sensor data into reliable, quality-assessed 3D ground-truth outputs. This is a principal-level technical leadership role for someone who can set the technical direction, build early prototypes, and align cross-functional teams around a shared reconstruction capability.



🙌 You should apply if you have:

Required Skills/Experience

 - Deep technical expertise in SLAM, 3D reconstruction, mapping, state estimation, or closely related robotics/perception fields.

 - Strong hands-on experience with lidar-based reconstruction, point-cloud registration, pose estimation, and real-world robotics sensor data.

 - Experience building offline reconstruction, mapping, or perception systems that operate on large volumes of sensor data.

 - Strong software engineering skills in C++, Python, or similar robotics/perception environments.

 - Experience taking research or prototype algorithms into reliable production systems.

 - Comfortable defining technical strategy, roadmaps, and milestones in ambiguous problem spaces

 - Strong cross-functional technical leadership in ambiguous, multi-team environments.

 - Clear communication of algorithmic tradeoffs, limitations, confidence, and failure modes to technical and cross functional stakeholders.

 - Systems-level understanding of sensor calibration, timing, synchronization and quality issues, and ability to define requirements and work with specialist teams to achieve them

Our Fleet Operations Team is responsible for maintaining the safety, performance, and operational readiness of Wayve's autonomous vehicle fleet — from routine servicing and diagnostics to urgent repairs and vehicle readiness for high-visibility events. The team keeps our fleet in peak condition to support testing, demonstrations, and real-world deployment, working closely with engineering, drivers, and operations teams to keep autonomy moving forward, every single day.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

Shift Leads are frontline operational leaders responsible for the safe, efficient, and high-performing execution of Wayve’s autonomous driving operations in Japan. You’ll ensure daily operations are conducted with the highest levels of safety and efficiency, and play a crucial role in fostering an inclusive working environment where Vehicle Safety Operators (VSOs) feel their ideas are valued and can voice safety concerns without fear. You’ll work directly within a cutting-edge autonomous vehicle testing environment, partnering with engineering, fleet operations, and automotive stakeholders to support real-world AI development.

We currently have two operational sites in Japan for on-road testing and development: one in Yokohama and one at Tokyo Ryutsu Centre, near Haneda Airport. This role will be mainly based in Tokyo Ryutsu Center, with occasional visits to Yokohama, offering exposure to a wide range of testing and operational activities.

This is a dedicated shift role with two shifts: morning (06:30–15:30) and night (14:30–23:30). We’ll do our best to accommodate your shift preferences, but we can’t always guarantee your first choice. Flexibility outside standard hours may occasionally be required to support testing activities, customer operations, or critical operational events. As Wayve scales in Japan, the role offers a pathway into broader operations, program management, and leadership responsibilities.

Operations run 7 days a week, so depending on your shift, you may need to work weekends and holidays. To compensate, we provide additional special paid leave for employees on the shift schedule.

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

You’ll lead a team of VSOs to deliver safe, high-quality, and efficient on-road testing operations.

 - Performance management: Line manage a group of VSOs working across a rostered shift pattern, with face-to-face, documented contact with each member at least monthly.

 - Customer engagement: Act as an operational point of contact for selected OEM and partner activities, ensuring smooth execution and professional stakeholder coordination.

 - Safety and compliance: Ensure all operations comply with company policies and legal regulations, and promote a safe work environment by enforcing safety protocols.

 - Quality control: Support high-quality data collection and testing execution by identifying operational issues, escalating risks, and maintaining testing standards.

 - Problem solving: Make real-time operational decisions in fast-moving environments, balancing safety, efficiency, and testing priorities.

 - Communication: Serve as the operational lead during shift hours, ensuring clear communication and coordination across Fleet Operations and cross-functional teams.

 - Reporting and documentation: Maintain accurate operational reporting, incident documentation, and shift handovers to support continuous improvement and operational visibility.

 - Incident management: Be the initial point of contact for an on-road incident and initial “Operations Officer” under the company Major Incident Management Plan.

 - Training and development: Coordinate individual and collective training and development events with the Quality Assurance team.

 - Continuous improvement: Identify opportunities to improve operational processes, utilisation, and team effectiveness as Wayve scales in Japan.

Essential:

 - You’re fluent in English and Japanese.

 - You stay calm, decisive, and professional in fast-paced operational environments, with sound judgement under high pressure.

 - You’re open to feedback and continuously seek to improve your performance and leadership skills.

 - You enjoy working with people and thrive in a team environment.

 - You have proven experience as a team coordinator or similar role in fast-moving environments (mobility, logistics, transportation, aviation, hospitality, field operations, etc.).

 - You have strong communication and stakeholder management skills across frontline teams and cross-functional partners.

 - You can work under pressure and manage multiple priorities, with excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

 - You’re proficient in Google Workspace or Microsoft Office.

 - All applicants are required to disclose any second job as part of the application process.

 - All applications are subject to a health check before/after.

Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. postings.description:

Simulation is a mission-critical part of how we build Wayve's driving intelligence. It lets teams evaluate changes faster, investigate failures and build confidence in the driving stack before it reaches the road.

Wayve's end-to-end driving stack creates a distinctive simulation challenge. There are no intermediate stages where simulated signals can be injected, so simulation has to be end to end too: reproducing the behaviour of a learned driving system across sensor data, model inference, routing, control and vehicle dynamics. Our simulator needs to be realistic enough to give meaningful signal, reproducible enough for teams to trust the results, and descriptive enough to explain the differences between simulated and on-road behaviour.

You'll join the Core Simulation team. Our open-loop and closed-loop workflows share one codebase, with different components configured depending on the use case. We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Safety System Engineer



🛠️ About our Engineering Teams



At Wayve, we are developing AV2.0: an end-to-end AI driving system designed to learn and adapt across a wide range of driving environments, with the ambition to scale autonomy globally. Our Safety team tackles one of the most important and complex challenges in that mission - assuring the safety of our Automated Driving System (ADS) as it evolves across vehicle platforms, applications and operating environments. You will help design and orchestrate the safety assurance framework that makes this possible.



🧠 Your day-to-day



You will lead functional safety activities for Wayve's ADS and its integration into current and future vehicle platforms, as well as third-party safety-critical systems. Working closely with internal engineering teams, external partners and other safety experts, you will build a deep understanding of the system, assess risk, shape the safety concept and architecture, define verification and validation, and develop the evidence needed to support a robust safety case.



🧩 What you’ll be working on:



• Build and maintain Item Definition work products for each vehicle platform and safety-critical integration.

• Conduct HARAs, FMEAs and FTAs to identify risk and define safety concepts that reduce risk to an acceptable level.

• Work with design teams on system architectures that satisfy the safety concept, including decomposition decisions and derived software and external requirements.

• Support software teams in implementing safety requirements on target hardware.

• Define test specifications across integration levels, including vehicle-level verification and validation of the safety concept.

• Build structured safety cases using clear claims, arguments and evidence.

How do we know when an AI Driver is ready for a fully driverless Robotaxi service? Our Product Architecture & Safety team brings together data, systems thinking and engineering expertise to help answer that question.

Working closely with Model Development, Behavioural Validation, Safety and Robotaxi Engineering, you’ll turn real-world driving, validation and operational data into evidence of what the Wayve AI Driver can do today—and what needs to improve next. Your work will help shape development priorities and measure progress towards a safe, reliable and scalable driverless service.

🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll take ownership of hands-on analysis, from exploring complex datasets in Python and SQL to sharing findings that guide product and engineering decisions.

 - Investigate driving behaviours and operational events to understand where, why and how often the system falls short of driverless service expectations.

 - Build practical metrics, performance baselines and dashboards to track progress across model, software and product releases.

 - Apply statistical methods to assess rare events, quantify uncertainty and distinguish meaningful improvements from noise.

 - Work with teams across Wayve to turn findings into development priorities, targeted validation and better data collection.

 - Contribute to product readiness reviews with clear evidence of progress, remaining limitations and the confidence behind your conclusions.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

 - Separating performance gaps from missing capabilities: Identify where better model performance can help and where additional system or product capabilities are needed.

 - Measuring the complete Robotaxi experience: Define metrics for remote assistance, passenger pickup and drop-off, passenger interactions, vehicle readiness and recovery from operational disruptions.

 - Evaluating service reliability: Measure intervention demand, mission completion, recovery time and vehicle availability to understand what it takes to deliver a dependable driverless service.

 - Exploring challenging scenarios: Investigate safety-critical interventions, unnecessary stops, stuck scenarios and manoeuvre execution across different roads and operating conditions.

 - You can turn an ambiguous real-world problem into measurable questions, useful KPIs and a practical analytical approach.

 - You’ve analysed complex systems, uncovered performance limitations and translated your findings into product or engineering improvements.

 - You understand statistical confidence, rare-event analysis, performance distributions and trends.

 - You’re comfortable working independently with incomplete data, making reasonable assumptions and refining your approach as new evidence emerges.

 - You communicate clearly with engineering, product and leadership stakeholders, explaining both your findings and their limitations.

Experience in autonomous driving, ADAS, robotics, mobility services or another complex physical system would be valuable. postings.title: Senior Sensor Technology Engineer
postings.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.



We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.



Here’s what this particular role covers.



🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

You’ll join Wayve’s Product & Delivery (P&D) organization, working within the Sensor Architecture team to help define and integrate the sensor systems behind our end-to-end autonomy stack.

The team works across the full sensor suite, with particular depth in camera systems, while also shaping radar, lidar and other sensing topics across customer and vehicle programs.

You’ll work closely with Wayve’s hardware and software teams, OEMs, Tier 1s and sensor suppliers, helping connect what sensors can physically deliver with how the Wayve AI Driver performs in real-world driving conditions.

This role sits at the intersection of sensor technology, vehicle integration and autonomous-driving performance, with responsibility for taking defined sensor topics from analysis through to clear, data-backed technical recommendations.



🧠 Your day-to-day

You’ll help translate driving use cases, ODD requirements and product constraints into clear sensor-system requirements and measurable KPIs such as coverage, field of view, resolution, detection range and latency.

A significant part of your work will focus on camera systems. You’ll contribute to camera concepts, module and sensor selection, variants, field of view, placement and integration requirements across different vehicle platforms.

You’ll evaluate and help tune image quality across areas such as exposure, HDR, ISP behaviour, LED flicker, low-light performance and image artefacts, working closely with Wayve’s hardware team and camera / ISP suppliers.

You’ll also work directly with OEMs and Tier 1s on camera mounting and vehicle-integration requirements, including position, alignment and tilt tolerances, mount rigidity, windshield and cover-glass effects, occlusion, heating and cleaning, synchronisation and calibration assumptions.

Beyond cameras, you’ll contribute to radar and lidar topics, supporting requirements definition, sample evaluation and integration discussions around areas such as mounting, radome and fascia effects, calibration and interference.

You’ll analyze fleet, replay and validation data to understand gaps between expected and observed sensor behaviour, define test requirements with the hardware team, review results and recommend next steps.

The role also includes hands-on work in the lab and on vehicles, supporting sensor bring-up and integration debugging when needed, as well as using Python to automate analysis and reporting.



🧩 What you’ll be working on:

 - Defining sensor-system requirements and quantitative KPIs derived from driving use cases, ODD and product constraints.

 - Developing camera-system concepts across sensor/module selection, variants, FOV and placement.

 - Evaluating camera image quality, including exposure, HDR, ISP, LED flicker, low-light performance and common image artefacts.

 - Defining camera mounting and vehicle-integration requirements for OEMs and Tier 1s.

 - Ensuring sensor characteristics, installation assumptions and calibration requirements remain consistent across development and production programs.

 - Analyzing fleet, simulation, replay and validation data to understand sensor performance and its impact on system KPIs.

 - Defining test requirements, reviewing results and supporting hands-on lab and vehicle testing.

 - Supporting sensor bring-up and hardware/software integration debugging.

 - Working directly with camera, radar and lidar suppliers on technical requirements, sample evaluation and integration constraints.

 - Supporting radar integration topics including mounting, radome/fascia effects and interference.

 - Supporting lidar and other sensing technologies such as ultrasonics where required.

 - Answering technical camera and sensor questions from customers and partners.

 - Maintaining sensor requirements, imaging guidelines, test specifications and technical recommendations.

 - Automating sensor-data analysis and reporting using Python.

 - Helping identify production and manufacturability constraints early as customer programs move from development toward production.
   
   

🙌 You should apply if:

 - 5+ years, of hands-on experience in automotive camera, radar or lidar engineering.

 - You have delivered technical work on automotive programs from requirements through integration, validation and verified results.

 - You have strong knowledge of camera systems, including image sensors, exposure, HDR, ISP pipelines, calibration and image artefacts.

 - You have practical experience with camera integration, image quality, sensor characterisation or ADAS sensor validation.

 - You have working knowledge of radar and/or lidar fundamentals and their vehicle-integration constraints, and can lead first-level technical discussions with suppliers.

 - You have experience defining camera mounting and integration requirements with OEMs or Tier 1s, including alignment tolerances, windshield or cover-glass effects, occlusion and mount rigidity.

 - You have used measurement and data analysis to make technical decisions, including image-quality evaluation using standard charts, tools and methods.

 - You are comfortable working across both hardware and software teams and directly with suppliers, OEMs and customers.

 - You can use Python or MATLAB for engineering analysis, automation and reporting.

 - You can write clear requirements, test specifications and concise, data-backed recommendations.

 - You enjoy working independently within a defined technical area and taking ownership from analysis through recommendation.

 - You are curious about how sensor behaviour affects autonomous-driving performance and are interested in broadening your expertise across camera, radar and lidar.

Experience with production ADAS or AV programs, mass-production sensor integration, ML-based perception, fleet-data analysis, replay-based validation, radome/fascia evaluation, IEEE P2020 concepts, ultrasonic sensors, SerDes, sensor configuration or synchronisation would be a strong advantage.

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

postings.description:

Wayve Labs develops the next generation of learning capabilities for embodied AI, using autonomous driving as a demanding real-world testbed. Within FORGE, our Language & Reasoning team explores how LLMs, VLMs and VLAs can connect world knowledge, grounded reasoning, memory and planning to physical action. We work across model architectures, training and post-training, with the goal of helping driving agents generalise to new environments, follow goals and constraints, and handle rare situations. The team collaborates across London and Sunnyvale, with opportunities to publish fundamental research.



🧠 Your day-to-day

You will set and lead an ambitious research agenda at the intersection of LLMs, VLMs, VLAs and embodied AI, asking how agents can use world knowledge, visual understanding, memory and reasoning to make better decisions in the physical world.

You will remain hands-on: developing new architectures and learning methods, training and evaluating large-scale models, and testing whether better reasoning leads to better behaviour in challenging driving scenarios.

As a Principal Research Scientist, you will guide the technical direction of the team, mentor researchers, build strong collaborations with Engineering, and turn original ideas into rigorous evidence, influential publications and capabilities that shape Wayve's next generation of AI.



🧩 What you’ll be working on:

 - Advance multimodal foundation models: Research and develop LLMs, VLMs and VLAs that integrate visual understanding, language, reasoning and action for embodied decision-making.

 - Develop reasoning and planning capabilities: Explore structured and latent reasoning, long-horizon planning, temporal understanding, memory, self-reflection and test-time computation for physically grounded agents.

 - Push the boundaries of model training: Develop scalable training and post-training methods, including supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, reward modelling, distillation and learning from human or AI-generated feedback.

 - Build steerable and adaptable policies: Enable embodied agents to understand instructions, follow goals and preferences, reason about constraints and generalise to novel environments and situations.

 - Explore agentic and hierarchical architectures: Investigate how deliberative reasoning, memory, external tools and fast reactive policies can work together, balancing intelligence, reliability and real-time constraints.

 - Bridge reasoning and action: Develop approaches that turn semantic understanding and reasoning into meaningful improvements in physical-world behaviour, rather than treating language generation as an end in itself.

 - Drive research from idea to evidence: Design rigorous experiments, build prototypes, establish challenging evaluations and demonstrate improvements in real-world capabilities.

 - Shape the research direction: Work closely with researchers across foundation models, representation learning, world modelling and reinforcement learning. Contribute original ideas, mentor others and help define the next generation of embodied AI systems.

 - A strong research track record in deep learning, particularly in one or more of LLMs, VLMs, VLAs, multimodal foundation models or embodied AI.

 - Hands-on experience developing, training, fine-tuning or post-training large-scale models, with a solid understanding of the challenges involved.

 - Strong knowledge of modern learning methods, such as instruction tuning, reinforcement learning, preference optimisation, reward modelling or reasoning-oriented post-training.

 - Excellent understanding of machine learning fundamentals, combined with the ability to challenge existing approaches and develop novel research ideas.

 - Strong practical skills in Python, PyTorch and large-scale machine learning experimentation.

 - Demonstrated ability to independently lead ambitious research projects, from identifying important problems to developing solutions and validating their impact.

 - A PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Robotics or a related field, or equivalent research experience, with a strong publication record or evidence of impactful research contributions.

postings.title: Senior Robotics Engineer - Offline Sensor Calibration
postings.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.



We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.



Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

We’re building reliable, repeatable calibration capabilities for Wayve’s vehicles. Our work ensures sensors are correctly installed and calibrated when a vehicle is set up, providing a dependable starting point for the online calibration systems that operate during driving.

As a senior engineer, you’ll take ownership of a developing area, from algorithm and tooling design through to physical setup and deployment. Working across cameras, LiDAR, radar and IMUs, you’ll turn calibration algorithms into practical workflows that can be validated and repeated across vehicle platforms and scaled across facilities in different regions.



🧠 YOUR DAY-TO-DAY

 - Own problems from investigation and design through implementation, validation and operational handover.

 - Collaborate with teams across robotics, operations, product and infrastructure to integrate and deploy calibration software and physical setups.

 - Translate calibration methods into reliable tools and repeatable workflows for use with physical hardware.


🧩 WHAT YOU’LL BE WORKING ON

 - Develop in-house, target-assisted software for end-of-line calibration of vehicle sensors.

 - Design and implement physical calibration setups across multiple geographies, selecting suitable targets, rigs and supporting tools for each location.

 - Develop checks to verify sensor installation and initial calibration, and identify sensors that may be misaligned or out of calibration.

 - Validate calibration accuracy and repeatability across vehicle platforms and sensor configurations, defining clear quality checks and operating procedures.

 - Help scale calibration setups and workflows to additional facilities and regions.

 - Contribute to offline robotics enrichment in the cloud data pipeline, including multi-bundle adjustment methods that improve calibration signals for model training.


🙌 YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

You bring strong hands-on experience in sensor calibration and can turn technical methods into reliable tools and repeatable workflows.


ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS

 - Sensor calibration: You have experience developing or applying calibration methods for cameras, LiDAR, radar or IMUs, ideally in a multi-sensor system.

 - Calibration geometry: You have a strong understanding of sensor models, coordinate frames, extrinsic calibration and geometric transformations.

 - Algorithms and optimisation: You have experience with optimisation-based methods used in calibration, such as bundle adjustment, least squares or factor graphs.

 - Software engineering: You have strong programming skills in Python and/or C++, with experience building maintainable, well-tested tools.

 - Validation and quality: You can define and apply meaningful checks for calibration accuracy, repeatability and sensor installation quality.

 - Practical implementation: You have experience taking algorithms from development into tools or workflows used with physical hardware.

 - Collaboration and ownership: You can work independently, take problems through to deployment and collaborate effectively with teams across locations and disciplines.


DESIRABLE EXPERIENCE

 - Experience designing or operating target-assisted calibration setups, including target selection, rig design or facility layout, is a plus.

 - Experience with end-of-line calibration, vehicle commissioning or calibration workflows for autonomous vehicles or robotics platforms is a plus.

 - Familiarity with multi-bundle adjustment, SLAM, state estimation or sensor fusion is a plus.

 - Experience contributing to offline data processing or cloud-based robotics pipelines is a plus.

 - Experience creating operator-facing calibration tools, diagnostics or visualisation is a plus.

The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.
